_id: feat025 with the Monte-Carlo consistency ensemble run at the FULL 3600 s arc instead of the 900 s default. This is the TREATMENT half of the pair whose other half is scene008mc: the two differ in estimation.multipathBias.useInEKF and in nothing else.
_delta: report.monteCarlo.enable true (was false) and duration_s 3600 (golden_baseline ships 900). nSeeds 12 and confidence 0.99 inherited unchanged.
_WHATTHEPAIRMEASURES: Whether carrying the tau = 60 s ground code multipath as a Gauss-Markov state, instead of charging its steady-state variance to R as though it were white, moves the POSITION NEES towards its acceptance band. NIS is expected to barely move, because R already charges the multipath at the correct marginal variance. A large NEES change against a flat NIS is the signature that the defect is the COLOUR of the error and not its size.
_READTHECOSTTOO: The expected accuracy result is that the converged position error gets WORSE, because the baseline number was partly bought by the filter over-trusting its code rows. Report both halves or the rung is misleading.
_WHYNOTTHE900sDEFAULT: Same reasoning as scene008mc and best002mc: burnInFraction 0.5 is not configurable, so 900 s pools a transient while 3600 s pools the regime the converged metric lives in.
